chunks: They will not fight you in a body except in fortified cities, or from behind the walls. Their enmity among themselves is great. You think they are united, but divided are their hearts. That is because these people are devoid of sense.
ai.seo_question: Why do the disbelievers appear united in battle but are actually divided?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Imran is often interpreted as a strategic observation of the Quraysh and other polytheists, highlighting that their apparent unity in battle was superficial, masking deep-seated tribal rivalries and a lack of true intellectual conviction (ya'sil). It serves as a lesson on the fragility of coalitions built on temporary interests rather than genuine faith, a theme frequently cited by Imams to explain the eventual fragmentation of opposing forces.
